@EraMacolli Thank you for sharing your perspective. As a Muslim, I deeply respect Prophet Jesus (ʿĪsā, peace be upon him). The Qur'an teaches that he is among the greatest messengers of Allah, born miraculously to Mary, and that he called people to worship God alone. 
 
However, the Qur'an also teaches that no human being—even a prophet—has the power to forgive sins or set people spiritually free by himself. Every prophet guided people to Allah, but ultimate forgiveness and salvation belong to Allah alone. 
 
Allah says: 
 
> "Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills."(Qur'an 4:48) 
 
And He says: 
 
> "Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.'"(Qur'an 39:53) 
 
Regarding Jesus (peace be upon him), the Qur'an records his own words: 
 
> "Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is the straight path."(Qur'an 3:51; see also 19:36) 
 
On the Day of Judgment, Allah will ask Jesus whether he told people to worship him and his mother. Jesus will reply: 
 
> "I said nothing to them except what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.'"(Qur'an 5:117) 
 
So, from the Islamic perspective, true freedom comes through knowing Allah, worshipping Him alone, sincerely repenting to Him, and following the guidance brought by all His prophets—including Jesus (peace be upon him) and Muhammad ﷺ. 
 
May Allah guide us all to the truth and increase us in humility, sincerity, and mutual respect.
